name: Ramp
text: Set a 48×48 px minimum touch target for all interactive elements. This ensures fat-finger safety and WCAG compliance without bloating the UI. The trade-off is slightly larger spacing, but that improves scanability and reduces accidental taps.

name: Reader
text: A 48×48 px touch target risks crowding small interactive elements—like buttons in tight toolbars—where it could force awkward scaling or truncate labels. A better alternative is a 44×44 px minimum (WCAG’s lower bound) with 4 px padding around labels, letting us keep density while maintaining safety. Test it with real users on small screens; if error rates spike, widen the targets.

name: Reader
text: A 44×44 px touch target with 4 px padding still risks crowding labels in dense UIs—especially when multiple buttons sit side by side. The real risk is truncation or overlapping text, which harms readability and usability. A better alternative is a 48×48 px minimum with 2 px padding, preserving WCAG compliance while keeping labels intact. Settle it by testing a toolbar with 3–4 buttons at both sizes to measure accidental taps versus label clarity.
